items.stem: State any three reasons for the growth of an enterprise.
items.answer: Economies of scale; Survival in competition; Higher profit; Larger market share; Spreading risk; Ambition of the entrepreneur

items.stem: Chopra Industries, a dairy in Dehradun, offers discounts to sell more milk to its existing customers. Which growth strategy is being used?

items.stem:

items.answer: (i) (a) Market penetration; (b) market development; (c) product development; (d) diversification. (ii) Economies of scale / spreading risk / higher profit / larger market share.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) (a) Market penetration; (b) market development; (c) product development; (d) diversification. (ii) Economies of scale / spreading risk / higher profit / larger market share.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Downward stretching"?
items.answer: Adding lower-priced items to a product line.
items.markingKey: (d) Downward stretching: Adding lower-priced items to a product line.
options: Adding new items to an existing product line.
Increasing the worth of a product through processing, packaging, branding or service so that customers pay more for it.
Adding new varieties, flavours or sizes under the same brand.
Adding lower-priced items to a product line.

items.stem: A farmer in Agra turns her tomatoes into ketchup and sells it at a higher price. How is value being added or the product line expanded? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Processing. Raw produce is processed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Processing; 2 marks for the justification: Raw produce is processed.

items.stem:
Fatima wants to open a juice bar in Varanasi. She is choosing between starting her own brand and taking a franchise of a well-known juice chain that charges an initial fee and a royalty of 6% on sales.
(i) State three advantages of taking the franchise. (ii) State two limitations.
items.answer: (i) Proven brand; training and support; lower risk; benefit of national advertising (any three). (ii) Fees and royalty; restrictions on products and prices; risk from other outlets harming the brand (any two).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Proven brand; training and support; lower risk; benefit of national advertising (any three). (ii) Fees and royalty; restrictions on products and prices; risk from other outlets harming the brand (any two).

items.stem: Explain "Access to new markets" with reference to the reasons for mergers and acquisitions.
items.answer: Access to new markets: The buyer gains the other firm's customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: The buyer gains the other firm's customers.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. A car company appoints a dealer in Coimbatore to sell its cars under its name. (a) Which type of franchising is shown? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Product or trade-name franchising (b) The franchisee sells the franchisor's products.
items.markingKey: (a) Product or trade-name franchising, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: The franchisee sells the franchisor's products.

items.stem: Explain "Branding" with reference to the ways of adding value to a product.
items.answer: Branding: A trusted name lets the firm charge more.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: A trusted name lets the firm charge more.

items.stem:
Rahul's bakery is popular in one area of Mumbai. He wants to grow quickly without investing much of his own money.
(i) Suggest an external growth method and give two reasons.
items.answer: (i) Franchising (or a strategic alliance): fast expansion; little own capital needed; uses franchisees' resources and local knowledge.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Franchising (or a strategic alliance): fast expansion; little own capital needed; uses franchisees' resources and local knowledge.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Royalty"?
items.answer: A continuing fee, usually a percentage of sales, paid by the franchisee to the franchisor.
items.markingKey: (a) Royalty: A continuing fee, usually a percentage of sales, paid by the franchisee to the franchisor.
options: A continuing fee, usually a percentage of sales, paid by the franchisee to the franchisor.
The firm that owns the brand and business system and grants the franchise.
The person or firm that buys the right to operate under the franchisor's brand.
An initial one-time payment made by the franchisee for the right to operate.

items.answer: (i) Proven brand; training and support; lower risk; benefit of national advertising (any three). (ii) Fees and royalty; restrictions on products and prices; risk from other outlets harming the brand (any two).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Proven brand; training and support; lower risk; benefit of national advertising (any three). (ii) Fees and royalty; restrictions on products and prices; risk from other outlets harming the brand (any two).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about value addition and product lines is correct?
items.answer: Adding new flavours under the same brand is line extension.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: Adding new flavours under the same brand is line extension.
options: Product-line expansion means removing products from the line.
Adding new flavours under the same brand is line extension.
Downward stretching adds premium products.
Value addition always reduces the price of a product.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. A shoe manufacturer merges with a chain of shoe stores. (a) Which type of merger is it? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Vertical merger (b) Production and retail stages combine.
items.markingKey: (a) Vertical merger, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Production and retail stages combine.
